claims.statement: The fragment describes opening Copilot Chat through the VS Code title-bar chat icon. It gives an entry action only, not sign-in, subscription eligibility, model selection, a transmitted prompt, or active session evidence.

The GitHub fragment describes opening the Chat panel from the Copilot icon beside search, resizing it from its top or left edge, and using the plus icon for a new conversation when a previous one appears. Starting a new UI conversation does not establish deletion of the previous conversation, changed retention, or any agent execution.

The pinned list resolves to GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.4, and GPT-5.4 nano using the source variable definitions. It lists model names without specifying plan, consumer availability, performance, current support, or permission to invoke them; the variable dependency is not newly reviewed as a whole.

The optional cloud-agent model selector describes choosing a model from a dropdown and choosing a reasoning level only when that model supports configurable reasoning. It links to further instructions without providing a full availability matrix, selection receipt, launch authorization, or current billing guarantee.

The optional GitHub agent selector describes choosing specialized profiles from repository, organization, or enterprise scope, or creating a profile in the selected repository and branch. Its included third-party-agent note describes paid-plan availability. Selection and paid eligibility are not evidence of enabled policies, permission to incur costs, reviewed tool capabilities, a created profile, or running agent; included and linked destinations are not newly certified here.

The generic fragment offers optional selection of a specialized custom agent from a dropdown and links to creation documentation. It provides no concrete profile, tool restrictions, approvals, selection receipt, or executed task, and does not itself authorize delegation.
